summary: PRISMA-style systematic review of 21 primary studies (2015-2026) that apply reinforcement learning to software vulnerability analysis, with emphasis on C/C++ and static analysis. Most studies use RL for fuzzing/exploration (15), few for detection (3) or statement-level localization (1). The authors identify the gap of RL agents using source-level CFGs as states.

claims.claim: 21 primary studies were identified; 15 focus on fuzzing/guided exploration, 3 on direct detection, 1 on statement-level localization.
claims.evidence: Table 2 and Fig. 1 PRISMA flow total 147 retrieved -> 83 after dedup -> 30 post-screen -> 29 full-text -> 21 included; RQ1 text names the 3 detection works (ProRLearn, DeepEXE, RLFD). The §2.4 prose says screening 'left 18 articles', which is inconsistent with the table's 30 post-screen.

claims.claim: Static structural representations (CFG/AST) are rarely used as agent state; no study uses source-level CFGs as state for detection/localization.
claims.evidence: RQ4 and Table 4: CFGs mostly from binaries (DeepEXE via IDA Pro); a single source-level CFG (Syzballer via SVF) is used to guide fuzzing. Bounded by a small search (four databases, ACM DL and arXiv not searched).

claims.claim: Benchmarks are heterogeneous and weakly comparable; few cross-project/unseen-CWE evaluations.
claims.evidence: RQ5/RQ6 qualitative synthesis over Table 5 datasets (LAVA-M, DARPA CGC, Juliet, Reveal, BigVul); no quantitative meta-analysis.

patterns.note: Surveys classic RL (DQN, PPO, bandits) for fuzzing and vulnerability detection, not RL for LLM coding agents.
Argues static-analysis-derived structure (CFG/AST) is underused as RL state; no evaluation.

methodology.sample: 147 records from Scopus, Web of Science, Taylor & Francis, IEEE Xplore and citation search; 21 included.
methodology.baselines: n/a (secondary study); Table 7 positions against prior reviews qualitatively.
methodology.models: n/a; RL algorithms surveyed (DQN variants in 8 studies, PPO in 3, UCB/MAB ~6, REINFORCE/VPG).
methodology.languages: C/C++ focus, with some binaries and multi-language datasets.

standards.peer_review: Submitted to CIARP 2026 (not yet accepted per arXiv comment).
standards.artifacts: No screening sheets, extraction forms or replication package released.
standards.preregistration: No registered protocol mentioned despite PRISMA claim.

biases.detail: 21 studies from a 147-record search; ACM Digital Library, arXiv and major security venues' proceedings are not listed as sources.
No description of multiple independent screeners or agreement statistics; no threats-to-validity section for the review itself.
§2.4 prose ('left 18 articles') disagrees with Table 2 (30 post-screen).

coi.affiliations: Universidad del Bío-Bío, Chile (master's student and two faculty).
coi.detail: Academic secondary study, no vendor ties.

verdict_reason: off-topic: classic RL for C/C++ fuzzing and vulnerability detection, not LLM agents or agent harnesses. It is also a small, unreplicable search with a prose/table count inconsistency and no threats section.
applicability: Does not transfer. The team works on Java backend ingestion and delivery with LLM coding agents, while this paper covers DQN/PPO fuzzers and detectors for C/C++ binaries and sources. It informs no decision about instruction files, verifier loops, multi-repo coordination, mixed hosts or spec-driven development. At most it suggests that off-the-shelf static analyzers (not RL detectors) remain the practical security check for the team.
